header:
What difference does paying
**weekly** make on a car loan?
footer: ASSUMES interest charged daily, no fees
notes: Simple interest accrued daily at 6.5%/365 on the balance; each payment covers accrued interest first, the rest pays principal. Monthly $587 (the 60-month payment on $30,000 at 6.5% is $586.98): 60 payments, interest $5,218.90 → $5,219. Biweekly $293.50 every 14 days: 119 payments, day 1,666 = 54.8 months (paid off in month 55), interest $4,671.47 → $4,671; saves 5,218.90 − 4,671.47 = $547.43 → −$547. Weekly $146.75 every 7 days: 237 payments, day 1,659 = 54.5 months (month 55), interest $4,649.86 → $4,650; saves $569.04 → −$569. Weekly vs biweekly: 4,671.47 − 4,649.86 = $21.61 → ≈ $22. Working: $587 × 12 = $7,044; $293.50 × 26 = $7,631; $146.75 × 52 = $7,631; $7,631 ÷ $587 = 13 exactly (one extra monthly payment a year). Biweekly gets 547.43 / 569.04 = 96% of weekly's saving with half as many payments, hence winner = biweekly.
